items.label: Mitochondria-targeted agents (class) × chronic heart failure
items.rationale: Only quantitative anchor is a phase-2-labeled meta-analysis with significant LVEF, NYHA, mortality, hospitalization benefits but unconfirmed GDMT comparator [42440741]; remaining records are narrative reviews without effect estimates [42022751, 40845481, 41595638, 42746169, 42609595]; GDMT exists as robust standard therapy.

items.label: AAV gene therapy (ND4/ND6) × Leber hereditary optic neuropathy
items.rationale: Phase-1 meta-analysis (n=175) shows significant BCVA improvement without treatment-related deaths but no responder-rate gain [42131170]; preclinical AAV2-ND6 restored visual function in mice without systemic toxicity [42709484]; idebenone remains standard, no head-to-head comparison.

items.label: PMD interventional therapies (class) × primary mitochondrial diseases
items.rationale: Late-stage trials 'negative or inconclusive' [42361626] cap effect_direction at 3; antioxidant/metabolic meta 'largely negative or mixed' [42630618]; broad pipeline (159 registered, 110 interventional) [42361626], four licensed agents [4265043]; supportive-care standard of care.

items.label: Elamipretide × primary mitochondrial diseases
items.rationale: Single case report (n=1): sustained clinical improvement and transplant-list inactivation [40816230]; commentary notes two FDA approvals in one year [42229401]. No controlled efficacy data; supportive care is the only standard; injectable formulation limits translatability.

items.label: Urolithin A × chronic heart failure
items.rationale: Two independent preclinical studies show consistent positive direction on remodeling, diastolic function, fibrosis [42432192, 42616901], but no human data, no significant p-values, no registered trials in set; GDMT partially covers the HF standard of care.

items.label: NAD+ precursors (NR/NMN) × unspecified disease (aging)
items.rationale: NAD+ precursor meta-analysis reports biomarker elevation but 'clinical benefits remain variable and context-dependent' [42489969]; primary data murine only (n=11) [42582917]; source record's disease label unclear, limiting unmet-need scoring.

items.label: MitoQ × Leber hereditary optic neuropathy
items.rationale: Thin evidence base: single meta-analysis, visual outcomes unreported (direction unclear) [42535808]; <2 ref_ids caps total at 4.0. Idebenone remains standard of care; oral formulation is a translational plus.

items.label: MitoQ × chronic heart failure
items.rationale: Meta-analysis could not assess MitoQ efficacy in HF (direction unclear) [42495453]; only support preclinical (mtROS, MMP, anti-inflammasome, no p-values) [42479041]; no posted human HF results; GDMT is a strong existing standard of care.

outsiders: MitoQ × chronic heart failure (3.1): efficacy unassessable in the meta-analysis [42495453]; preclinical signals lack reported p-values [42479041]; robust GDMT standard of care exists.
MitoQ × Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (3.3): thin evidence base — single meta-analysis with unreported visual outcomes [42535808]; total capped at 4.0 per rubric.
caveats: No convincing leaders yet: top total 5.8 < 6.0; the only quantitative anchor is a single phase-2-labeled meta-analysis with an unconfirmed GDMT comparator [42440741].
PMD class effect_direction capped at 3 for negative late-stage trial outcomes [42361626] and a largely negative/mixed meta-analysis [42630618].
MitoQ × LHON flagged 'thin evidence base' (1 ref_id) [42535808]; total capped at 4.0 (raw 3.3).

Preclinical directions were scored on surrogate outcomes without reported p-values [42479041, 42432192, 42616901]; single-study directions (luteolin [42013553], Calhex231 [42748783], DMM [42805426], MitoQ × septic cardiomyopathy [42460027]) excluded as thin bases.
NAD+ precursor direction: disease label 'unclear' [42489969], murine-only primary data (n=11) [42582917], NAD+ biomarker is a surrogate endpoint.
No record has is_standard_of_care=true and none reports a comparator arm's own effect; the standard-of-care side is defined only by the SOC map.
